### THE FINDING — a hand-duplicated body that should have been a call

`fn_3_47628` (336 B, 99.82143%) is a real, `global`, no-argument function that scans runners 3..0 and returns a cutoff target base. **It has no `bl` caller anywhere in the module** — MWCC INLINES it at its call sites while still emitting the out-of-line body, because it is non-static. Our source had hand-duplicated that body into TWO other places instead of calling it: a private `static findCutoffTargetBase()` in `autoMovement5` and ~40 inline lines in `fn_3_480B8`.

Replacing both with `fn_3_47628()` improved both and deleted ~75 lines of duplicated source. MWCC inlined it at both new call sites (verified: no `bl fn_3_47628` in either function's output).

**The duplication was also hiding two genuine decode bugs in `fn_3_480B8`**, both invisible while the body was duplicated:
- It wrote `baseToTarget = -1` at two sites where the target emits `li r0, 0x0` (target addrs 0x48164 and 0x481D8) — and the follow-up guard is `if (baseToTarget != -1)`, so this changed behaviour, not just codegen.
- It initialised `baseToTarget = 4` BEFORE the loop; the target emits `li r0, 0x4` AFTER the `bdnz` (target addr 0x48230), i.e. on the loop-completed-without-break path. That is exactly what `fn_3_47628`'s trailing `return 4;` produces once inlined. Session 30 had seen this as "the same instruction merely relocated" and attributed it to register colour.

**Generalisable rule: before grinding register colour on a function containing a block that also appears elsewhere in the file, check whether that block is a real function in the same TU that MWCC inlines. A `global` function with a body but zero `bl` callers in the module is the tell.**

### 4. setCatcherCatchStrategy_distToLandingSpot — the 44-byte gap is NOT a
### register-economy problem

**The framing given to this worker was wrong and it said so.** The task was to find
"the long-lived value wanting a fifth callee-saved register". There is no such value.

Target's r27 is written ONCE (`lwz r27,0x8(r1)`), holds the raw 32-bit bit pattern of
the FIRST `fielderSqrt` result read back through a stack round-trip, and is consumed
only by the ~9-instruction NaN/Inf/zero classification that immediately follows. Last
use 9 instructions later; never touched again except the epilogue `lmw`. It is a
compiler-internal artifact of the `fielderSqrt` expansion, not a source-level local.
It landed in a callee-saved register only because at that one program point nine
registers were already pinned (r6 frame, r7 startFrame delta, r9 the 9999 sentinel
constant, r10 best-frame, r11 found flag, r12 closeEnough flag, r29/r30/r31).

**We actually use one FEWER nonvolatile than target**: our `resultCode` lives in
volatile r9 the whole function, which target cannot do because target's r9 holds the
9999 constant (ours puts that in r8). Ours reuses nonvolatile r28 at BOTH sqrt classify
sites; target had a free volatile at the second site and never re-used r27 there.

**So the 44 bytes do NOT come from stmw/lmw economy.** They come from scattered
scheduling and addressing-mode differences. Do not chase the register count.

**Ranked hypotheses, NOT applied:**

1. **(High confidence, cheap) Remove the two `||` fusions.** Our object emits
   `cror eq,gt,eq` + one fused branch at both `if (found == 0 || bestHeight >= ...)`
   and `if (landingDist >= lbl_3_rodata_B78 || resultCode != 1)`; target emits two
   independent compare/branch pairs with no `cror` at either. Rewrite each as nested
   `if`/`else if`/`else` with the arms written out. Not previously tried — the
   checkpoint's excluded list covers the `cantCatchFlyBallInd` boolean idiom and the
   B68 polarity test, which are different conditions.
2. **(Medium) Match target's element-base addressing.** Target keeps r4 pointing at the
   whole `futureCoordsAndDist[frame]` element and reads `pos.x` at +0x354 / `pos.z` at
   +0x35c off it (using an `lfsu`), and separately computes and keeps
   `r5 = &futureCoord->pos.x`. Ours advances the pointer to `&futureCoord->pos` early
   (`addi r4,r4,0x354`) and indexes 0x0/0x4/0x8 off that narrower sub-object pointer.
   Introducing an explicit `f32* futureX = &futureCoord->pos.x;` may nudge the
   addressing-mode choice. Speculative.
3. **(Low, no concrete edit) Reproduce the register-pressure spike** at the first
   classify block by reordering/rescoping the dx/dz/dxSq/dzSq temporaries. Honest
   assessment from the worker: this is a "hope the allocator agrees" experiment.

Also noted: ours emits `srawi` where target emits `srwi` for
`fielder->maxAccLength_ConstF >> 1`. Bit-identical result since the field is u8, so not
a correctness bug, but a real instruction-selection difference at that source line.
And the `landingDist` sqrt site shows an FMA contraction difference (ours `fmadds`,
target separate `fmuls`+`fadds`) — **check the checkpoint before retrying: the logged
FMA exclusion covers the 1st and 3rd sqrt sites for a different expression shape and
may not cover this one.**

```c
void catchAnimationProgression(int fielderIndex) {
    InMemFielder* fielder = &g_Fielders[fielderIndex];
    f32 dx, dz;
    f32 dist;

    fielder->catchAnimationFramesCountDown--;
    fielder->catchAnimationFramesCountUp++;

    if (fielder->autoCatch0_noCatchAnimationOnly1) {
        if (fielder->catchAnimationFramesCountDown > 0) {
            return;
        }
        fielder->catchAnimation = 0;
        return;
    }

    if (g_Ball.fielderWBallIndex >= 0) {
        if (g_d_GameSettings.GameModeSelected != GAME_TYPE_TOY_FIELD &&
            fielderIndex != g_FieldingLogic.selectedFielder && fielderIndex != -1) {
            fielder->autoMovementFunctionIndex = 12;
            if (autoMovementFunctions[12].code >= 0) {
                g_FieldingLogic.fielderAutoMovementCode[fielderIndex] = autoMovementFunctions[12].code;
            }
            fielder->unknown_writeOnly = 0;
            fielder->fielderVeloAdjustmentCode = 0;
            fielder->unknown_writeOnly_always0 = 0;
            fielder->timeSinceThrowWasCaught = 0;
            fielder->fielderTrackingBallState = 0;
        }
        fielder->catchAnimation = 0;
        fielder->currentVelocity = lbl_3_rodata_B20;
        fielder->framesSinceThrowWasMade = 0;
        fielder->playerNeedsToMoveToCatchThrowInd = 0;
        fielder->fielderMadeThrow = 0;
        fielder->clamberStatus = 0;
        fielder->wallJumpStatus = 0;
        if (fielder->unknown_Unused != 0) {
            fielder->unknown_Unused = 2;
        }
        if (g_Ball.fielderWBallIndex >= 0 && g_Ball.catchAnimationTotalFrames != 0) {
            g_Ball.catchAnimationTotalFrames = 0;
            g_Ball.AtBat_Contact_BallPos.x = g_Ball.fielderActionCatchCoords.x;
            g_Ball.AtBat_Contact_BallPos.y = g_Ball.fielderActionCatchCoords.y;
            g_Ball.AtBat_Contact_BallPos.z = g_Ball.fielderActionCatchCoords.z;
        }
        return;
    }

    if (g_Ball.deadBallReason) {
        if (g_d_GameSettings.GameModeSelected != GAME_TYPE_TOY_FIELD &&
            fielderIndex != g_FieldingLogic.selectedFielder && fielderIndex != -1) {
            fielder->autoMovementFunctionIndex = 12;
            if (autoMovementFunctions[12].code >= 0) {
                g_FieldingLogic.fielderAutoMovementCode[fielderIndex] = autoMovementFunctions[12].code;
            }
            fielder->unknown_writeOnly = 0;
            fielder->fielderVeloAdjustmentCode = 0;
            fielder->unknown_writeOnly_always0 = 0;
            fielder->timeSinceThrowWasCaught = 0;
            fielder->fielderTrackingBallState = 0;
        }
        fielder->catchAnimation = 0;
        fielder->currentVelocity = lbl_3_rodata_B20;
        fielder->framesSinceThrowWasMade = 0;
        fielder->playerNeedsToMoveToCatchThrowInd = 0;
        fielder->fielderMadeThrow = 0;
        fielder->clamberStatus = 0;
        fielder->wallJumpStatus = 0;
        if (fielder->unknown_Unused != 0) {
            fielder->unknown_Unused = 2;
        }
        if (g_Ball.fielderWBallIndex >= 0 && g_Ball.catchAnimationTotalFrames != 0) {
            g_Ball.catchAnimationTotalFrames = 0;
            g_Ball.AtBat_Contact_BallPos.x = g_Ball.fielderActionCatchCoords.x;
            g_Ball.AtBat_Contact_BallPos.y = g_Ball.fielderActionCatchCoords.y;
            g_Ball.AtBat_Contact_BallPos.z = g_Ball.fielderActionCatchCoords.z;
        }
        return;
    }

    if (fielder->catchAnimationFramesCountDown > 0) {
        if (!fielder->caughtBallInAir) {
            return;
        }
        dx = g_Ball.physicsSubstruct.ballLandingSpotOrHeldSpot.x - fielder->pos.x;
        dz = g_Ball.physicsSubstruct.ballLandingSpotOrHeldSpot.z - fielder->pos.z;
        dist = fielderSqrt(dx * dx + dz * dz);
        if (dist < lbl_3_rodata_B64) {
            g_FieldingLogic._0144 = 1;
        }
        return;
    }

    g_FieldingLogic.dashPtr->sprintingState = 0;
    g_FieldingLogic.dashPtr->dashingFielderIndex = -1;
    g_FieldingLogic.dashPtr->framesSinceLastDashInput = -1;
    g_FieldingLogic.dashPtr->sprintLengthInFrames = -1;

    if (g_Ball.currentStarSwing == 1 || g_Ball.currentStarSwing == 2) {
        fielder->bobble = 4;
        bobbleDirection(fielderIndex);
        return;
    }

    if (fielder->bobble == 2 || fielder->bobble == 3) {
        bobbleDirection(fielderIndex);
        if (g_d_GameSettings.minigamesEnabled) {
            if (g_Minigame.minigameControlStruct[0].battingHandedness[fielder->_020D] == 0) {
                setCharacterAnimations(g_Minigame.minigameControlStruct[0].characterIndex[fielder->_020D], 0);
            }
        } else {
            if (g_GameLogic.teamIsCPU[g_GameLogic.teamFielding] == 0) {
                setCharacterAnimations(g_GameLogic.teamFielding, 0);
            }
        }
        return;
    }

    updateVariablesPostCatch(fielderIndex);

    if (fielder->bobble == 0 || fielder->bobble == 1) {
        if (g_d_GameSettings.minigamesEnabled) {
            if (g_Minigame.minigameControlStruct[0].battingHandedness[fielder->_020D] == 0) {
                setCharacterAnimations(g_Minigame.minigameControlStruct[0].characterIndex[fielder->_020D], 0);
            }
        } else {
            if (g_GameLogic.teamIsCPU[g_GameLogic.teamFielding] == 0) {
                setCharacterAnimations(g_GameLogic.teamFielding, 0);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### THE session-38 method finding: CANONICAL and PER-UNIT disagree on which functions are at 100%, and a whole round-trip was burned on the resulting phantom regression

A worker reported that `calculateBobble` and `initializeFielderConstants` had dropped
off the 100% set after the new implementation landed. A full bisect was commissioned.
The bisect reverted the function to a state **byte-identical to HEAD** and both
functions were STILL below 100% in that state — which is impossible if the session's
edit had caused it.

Root cause: the two measurement frames use different symbol tables and different
scores.
- PER-UNIT (`objdiff-cli diff -p . -u <unit> -o - --format json`) reports
  `calculateBobble` 99.92308% and `initializeFielderConstants` 99.87013%, and its
  table has ~228 entries because it INCLUDES DATA SYMBOLS.
- CANONICAL (`build/GYQE01/report.json`, from `report generate`, which also runs as
  the `[1/1] PROGRESS` step of a normal `ninja`) reports BOTH at exactly 100.0, and
  has 223 FUNCTION entries.

The giveaway that the comparison was invalid: the worker's "newly at 100%" list was
`autoMovementFunctions`, `currentStickDirection`,
`fielderControlStick_continuousAngleHistory` — all three are DATA symbols, not
functions. If a set difference reports data symbols as gained, you are comparing a
PER-UNIT table against a CANONICAL baseline and the result is meaningless.

**Rule: always compare like with like. Regression checks must be CANONICAL-vs-CANONICAL.**
This is the concrete, reproducible instance of the standing "label figures CANONICAL or
PER-UNIT" rule, and it cost a full round-trip. The difference is not a rounding
artifact — these two functions are genuinely scored differently by the two code paths,
almost certainly because of the known-fragile anonymous-`@N`-rodata-label identity
heuristic documented in the session-19 note on `lbl_3_rodata_B50` / `@2222`.

### CORRECTION to an established lever: the `extsh` tell does NOT mean "declare it narrow"

The standing lever says to check narrow-local width in both directions per the
`extsh`/`extsh.` tell. This session produced a clean counter-example. The target
demonstrably emits, at the three angle-helper call sites in `catchThrownBallFun`:
```
extsh  r30, r3     ; after bl normalizeAngle
extsh  r4,  r3     ; after bl calculateAngleFromCoordinates
extsh. r0,  r3     ; after bl angleDifferenceNormalized
```
Despite the target emitting the truncation, declaring the locals `s16` scored WORSE
than declaring them `int`:
- all three `s16`: 90.5% / 2152 B
- all three `int`: **92.10112% / 2148 B**  (KEPT)
- only `angleToTravel` s16: 91.24906% / 2148 B
- only `angleToEntry`  s16: 91.25843% / 2152 B
- only `angleDiff`     s16: 91.72659% / 2148 B

MWCC emits the equivalent narrowing from `int`-typed source anyway at the result of a
callee that returns `s16`, but schedules and colours it like the target. So the
presence of `extsh` in the target is NOT by itself evidence for a narrow declaration —
**measure both widths, and cross the individual locals, rather than reading the opcode
as the answer.** This does not overturn the lever for struct fields, where width is a
fact read off the access opcode; it applies to LOCALS only.

## setFielderCatchStrategy_calcFramesToGetToDropSpot (from-scratch implementation)

Baseline: `return;` stub, 0.11669%, target size 3428 B (0xD64).
Current state: full from-scratch implementation, exact size match (3428 B), 69.211205% per-unit.
Source: `src/game/fielding/fielder.c` lines ~13536-13827 (uncommitted working tree copy).

Signature: `void setFielderCatchStrategy_calcFramesToGetToDropSpot(int fielderIndex)` -- the
`void(void)` prototype was wrong, same as the sibling. Fixed in `fielder.h` and the definition.
No other src/ callers exist yet (the 3 call sites in target asm are inside other stub functions).

What it does: computes, for one fielder, which future ball-position frame to target as a
"catch/drop spot" and records catchStrategy / framesToGetToBallLandingSpot / etc. It is a third
variant in the knockoutRelated_subFn / setCatcherCatchStrategy_distToLandingSpot family, adding
an AI-level/minigame-dependent per-iteration frame step, a per-fielder dynamic height/lateness
threshold using distanceFromHomePlate, an outfielder-specific closeEnough refinement, an extra
forward-search sub-algorithm (two nested loops, outfielders with AILevel<=1 only), a foul-ball
override using howFoulTheBallWillBe/maxYOfHit, a post-loop catchStrategy rebucketing by landing
distance, and a materially different tail bitmask-set (angle+throw-time gated for
nonCatchFlyBallStratInd!=0, using an angle check absent from the siblings).

Decode findings (from the target/left side of objdiff-cli diff, confirmed via disassembly reads,
not guesses unless noted):
- g_d_GameSettings.minigamesEnabled (GameInitVariables+0x11) selects a simpler setup path
  (step=3, skips the whole AILevel switch and threshold override).
- fielder->AILevel3Weak0Powerful (0x1C4) switch sets the per-iteration step: 0->2, 1->3,
  default->5, 3->(g_Ball.StaticRandomInt1 % 3)+6, 4->(g_Ball.StaticRandomInt1 % 4)+8.
  g_Ball.StaticRandomInt1 is s32 at InMemBallType+0x1B4C (confirmed via lwz not lha).
- lbl_3_data_1C3C[0] (s16) is subtracted from frame in the main comparison
  (framesNeeded < frame - delayFrames), REPLACING the "-5" adjustment both siblings apply to
  framesNeeded directly. Confirmed: the same-position shortcut here sets framesNeeded=1 with no
  "-5" folded in anywhere -- a genuine behavioral divergence from both siblings, not a guess.
- For fielderIndex >= 6 in the non-minigame path, the per-frame height threshold is
  fielder->distanceFromHomePlate (f32, 0x70) - lbl_3_rodata_B24, not the constant lbl_3_rodata_B98
  the siblings use.
- The "ball already too low" break condition compares against fielder->distanceFromHomePlate
  (0x70), not the rodata constant lbl_3_rodata_B68 the siblings use for the equivalent check.
  lbl_3_rodata_B68 IS still used later for the post-loop resultCode==2 reclassification, matching
  the siblings exactly there.
- The flat frame+=3 "ball still too high" step from both siblings is replaced by a 3-tier check:
  +10 if pos.y > lbl_3_rodata_B9C, +6 if pos.y > lbl_3_rodata_BA0, else +3.
- closeEnough (framesNeeded < frame+30) is further gated for fielderIndex in [2,5]: also requires
  futureCoord->dist <= lbl_3_rodata_B64 + fielder->distanceFromHomePlate, OR framesNeeded <
  frame+10 as a fallback. Outside indices 2-5 it's unconditional. futureCoord->dist is
  CoordAndDist.dist, f32 at struct offset 0xC.
- New branch (absent from both siblings): when framesNeeded > lastFramesNeeded && found==0 &&
  AILevel<=1 && fielderIndex>=6 && lastFramesNeeded+15 > frame, runs a two-stage forward search
  (candidate offsets 5,10,...,70, 14-iteration loop breaking on first catchable offset; then a

## Durable finding (this pass)

A value living in a raw volatile register across an inlined helper's own internal scratch-
register usage is not the same failure mode as a value living across a real bl call. The
standing rule "a value live across a call needs a nonvolatile register" does not directly explain
why the target avoids spilling threshold/bestHeight here -- both sides fully inline fielderSqrt
(no bl fielderSqrt on either side), so there is no real call boundary. The target instead proves,
at the source's actual control-flow shape, that f0/f1 are dead at every point the inlined sqrt
expansion would otherwise clobber them (confirmed by reading the target .s directly: the sqrt
expansion inside the branch where bestHeight is live uses f1-f6 only, while a second,
textually-identical-looking sqrt expansion elsewhere in the same function -- in a branch where
bestHeight is provably not live -- freely uses f0 as scratch). Reshaping how the source caches
these two locals (recomputing instead of caching, reading back from the array instead of a
separate local) did not reproduce this register-allocation behavior and made things worse both
times. Before spending more budget on source-level reshaping of a spilled float, dump and compare
the actual register-allocated scratch usage inside the inlined helper expansion on both sides --
the fix may be closer to "restructure which branch computes the sqrt first" or "avoid a
computation order that keeps the value live across the expansion" than to the variable's
declaration style.

Session 39 flagged it as a puzzle that this function stayed at 0.2631579% after its sole
blocker (`setFielderCatchStrategy_calcFramesToGetToDropSpot`) stopped being a stub, and
speculated about a hidden joint blocker set. The real explanation is mundane and was already

```c
void humanTeamFieldingFirstFrameAfterHit(void) {
    return;
}
```
Unblocking a caller does not write the caller's body. There is no joint-blocker mystery and no
defect in the blocker model. The same applies to `aITeamFieldingFirstFrameAfterHit`, also still
a verbatim stub.

**Durable lesson, worth generalising:** before opening an investigation into "why didn't X move
after we unblocked it", check whether X is itself still a stub. An unblocked stub scores exactly
as badly as a blocked stub — the blocker model predicts nothing about a function whose body
hasn't been written. Cross-check the "did it move" question against the call graph's own stub
list, which already has the answer.

#### Durable finding: MWCC assigns `.bss` in REVERSE declaration order

This is the operative fact behind [4] and it closed the `.bss` section outright. The target's
section-relative `.bss` layout for this TU is:
```
0x00   lbl_3_bss_C8                                0xA4   local
0xA4   currentStickDirection                       0x02   local
0xA6   gap_05_0000016E_bss                         0x02   global, hidden
0xA8   fielderControlStick_continuousAngleHistory  0x90   local, data:2byte
0x138  (end)
```
To produce that, the source must declare them in the REVERSE of that order:
`fielderControlStick_continuousAngleHistory`, then `currentStickDirection`, then `lbl_3_bss_C8`.
This is consistent with the reverse-declaration-order note already in `docs/matching_notes.md`,
and is the `.bss` analogue of the `-inline deferred` reverse-emission rule for `.text`.

Two sub-findings worth keeping:
- **The 2-byte gap symbol needs no source declaration.** `gap_05_0000016E_bss` is generated by
  the decomp-toolkit from the TARGET binary's alignment gaps (`fill_gaps` in
  `config.example.yml`); it is not in `config/GYQE01/game/symbols.txt` and there is no
  gap-object idiom anywhere in `src/`. With the correct declaration order the 2-byte hole falls
  out of natural alignment on its own. Do not hand-declare gap symbols.
- **Folding sibling statics into one struct to force a shared base register is counterproductive**
  ([2]). It looks "more literally correct" against the disassembly's single-base-register
  addressing, but it raised register pressure and displaced the base pointer, scoring WORSE than
  leaving them as separate statics in the right order. Getting the ORDER right produced the
  folded `+0xA4`/`+0xA8` addressing anyway, for free.

### `humanTeamFieldingFirstFrameAfterHit` — stub -> **98.4079%** (1508 B vs target 1520 B)

Signature **confirmed correct as declared**: `void humanTeamFieldingFirstFrameAfterHit(void)`.
Header prototype at `include/game/fielding/fielder.h:89` was already right. Evidence: no parameter
register is used at entry; everything is read from globals, matching the already-implemented cousin
`fn_3_31A3C`.

Purpose: the human-team "first frame after the ball is hit" fielding setup. For each of the 9
fielders it recomputes `angleOfFieldersStartingPosition`, `distanceFromHomePlate` and
`distanceFromLandingSpot`, calls the appropriate catch-strategy setter
(`setCatcherCatchStrategy_distToLandingSpot(1)` for the catcher at index 1,
`setFielderCatchStrategy_calcFramesToGetToDropSpot(i)` otherwise), and packs a 3-bit-per-fielder
code for `catchStrategy in {1,2,3}` into a 64-bit `catchStrategyMask`. After the loop a
Practice-Batting special case resets the pitcher and returns early; otherwise the mask and ball
state select one of `selectInitialFielders_linedriveThroughPitcher`,
`setInitialFielderMovements_foulBall`, `setInitialFielderMovements_DeepFly`, or
`setInitialFielderMovements_generalCase` (plus `chooseSecondaryFielderFromClosestOutfielder`, an
auto-movement-code-22 block, and `CoverBases`/`cutoffs`/`restOfFielders`), before storing
`secondaryFielder`/`tertiaryFielder` into their `...Stored` shadow fields.

#### Notable: the target contains a real bug, faithfully reproduced
The inlined atan2-based angle formula adds `SANG_ANG_180` (0x800) on a negative result where
`SANG_ANG_360` is what the math calls for. This exact simplified-and-buggy variant already exists
verbatim in `fn_3_31A3C`, so it is the original developers' shared helper body, not a transcription
error. Do not "fix" it — it must be reproduced to match.

#### Durable finding: the `fielder++` pointer-walk is NOT always the right shape
This file's long-standing convention note says to prefer `InMemFielder* fielder = &g_Fielders[i];`
whenever the target materialises the base into a register. Hypothesis [15] is a measured
counter-example at loop scope: a *walking* pointer (`fielder = g_Fielders; ... fielder++;`) scored
WORSE than plain `g_Fielders[i]` indexing, and switching to indexing removed both the phantom
`mr r30,r0` copy and the r28/r27/r26-vs-r26/r28/r29 misallocation in one move (+0.30%). The
convention is about a base materialised ONCE for a single fielder, not about a loop that advances a
cursor across all 9. Distinguish the two cases before applying the rule.

Second durable point, from [3]: when the target packs bits into a 64-bit mask, doing the shift in
the **32-bit domain and sign-extending afterwards** (`(s64)(4 << shiftAmt)`) is materially better
than shifting in the 64-bit domain (`(s64)4 << shiftAmt`) -- +5.5% here. MWCC emits a full 64-bit
shift sequence for the latter.

Third, from [14]: `s16` for the loop counter cost 2.4% here. The "measure both int and s16" rule
stands, but in this function `int` won clearly.

- `InMemFielder.catchStrategy` (0x1DD, u8) drives the packing: 1 -> bit weight 4, 2 -> 2, 3 -> 1
  (i.e. `1 << (3 - catchStrategy)`), with no bit contributed for 0 or >= 4.
- `g_FieldingLogic.secondaryFielder`/`tertiaryFielder` (0xB2/0xB4) vs `...Stored` (0xB8/0xBA):
  THIS function is what writes the `Stored` shadow copies, at its very end.
- `g_Ball.landingSpotLocation` (VecXZ, 0x1A2C) is a DIFFERENT field from
  `g_Ball.ballLandingSpotOrHeldSpot` (VecXZ, 0x1C8). Both exist, both are used, by different

- `fielderSqrt` (`src/game/fielding/fielder.c:150`, wrapping `dolsqrtf2`) is the sqrt idiom for the
  whole file: any float distance calculation showing the frsqrte / Newton / NaN-classification
  ladder should be transcribed as a `fielderSqrt(...)` call, never hand-rolled.

### `fn_3_402A8` — stub -> **95.09516%** (2364 B vs target 2396 B)

Signature confirmed correct as declared: `void fn_3_402A8(void)` (no `mulli rN,r3,0x268` at entry).

Purpose: builds a 9-fielder bitmask of who has a viable fly-ball catch strategy
(`nonCatchFlyBallStratInd == 0`, bit `1 << (i*3)`). If a subset condition on that mask plus the
ball's landing zone/height holds, it tries to assign the catcher (fielder 1) to chase a shallow
popup; failing that it runs a distance/angle-threshold cascade assigning the pitcher (0) or one of
fielders 2/3/4/5 by landing angle. If no window matches it falls into a "farTail" path: if none of
the outfielders (6/7/8) are eligible it defers entirely to `fn_3_3FCF0`; otherwise it picks a
3-fielder outfield backup group by `Hit_HorizontalAngle` bucket, tie-breaking fielders 3 vs 5 by
straight-line distance in the widest bucket. Every terminal branch converges on
`setInitialFielderMovements_CoverBases`/`_cutoffs`/`_restOfFielders`.

Negative result worth recording: `setZoneAwayFromHome` is **NOT** the missed inline here. This
function's angle-bucket cascade is a flat sequence of hard-coded thresholds
(0x2c0/0x400/0x540/0x800/0x3c0/0x440), not that helper's ladder. The "consecutive rodata label
ladder => look for an existing in-file helper" heuristic was checked and correctly came back
negative — the heuristic is about *float* comparisons against adjacent rodata labels, and these are
*integer* angle thresholds. Don't over-apply it.

#### Rejected source shape: never encode a register coincidence as a type cast
A first draft wrote `fn_3_3FCF0((BOOL)ball);` — casting an `InMemBallType*` to a `BOOL` parameter —
purely to reproduce the target's `mr r3,r31`. Investigation: `fn_3_3FCF0`'s parameter is used
exactly once, as `if (useComputedAngle)`, and is never dereferenced, so the declared
`void fn_3_3FCF0(BOOL)` prototype is CORRECT and the pointer was never a pointer semantically. The
target really does emit `mr r3,r31` there, but only because `&g_Ball` is a conveniently non-NULL
truthy value already in a register. Writing `fn_3_3FCF0(TRUE);` is the honest form — **and it
scored BETTER** (95.020035% -> 95.03673%), because the register allocation elsewhere in the
function shifted favourably. Lesson: a cast that exists only to reproduce a register move is both
a lie about the code and frequently not even a win. Check the callee's actual parameter usage.

#### `goto` audit (per the standing last-resort rule)
6 gotos remain (3x `goto farTail`, 3x `goto tail`) and they ARE justified exit-block threading:
`farTail` is a large shared block reached from 3 independent conditions at different nesting
depths, and `tail` must be reachable both from the main angle cascade and by falling out of
`farTail`. The structured alternative was **measured**, not assumed: a `BOOL useFarTail` flag with
nested if/else and no labels scored 93.480804% / 2408 B — 1.56 points worse AND 44 bytes LONGER
than the target, where the goto form is 32 bytes shorter. Rejected on evidence.

### MAJOR durable finding: the file-wide auto-movement setter IS a `static inline`

The checkpoint has suspected since session 1 that this recurring 6-statement idiom was a
`static inline` setter in the original source. **Confirmed this session, by measurement.** Added:
```c
static inline void setFielderAutoMovement(int fielderIndex, int autoMovementIndex) {
    InMemFielder* f = &g_Fielders[fielderIndex];
    f->autoMovementFunctionIndex = autoMovementIndex;
    if (autoMovementFunctions[autoMovementIndex].code >= 0) {
        g_FieldingLogic.fielderAutoMovementCode[fielderIndex] = autoMovementFunctions[autoMovementIndex].code;
    }
    f->unknown_writeOnly = 0;
    f->fielderVeloAdjustmentCode = 0;
    f->unknown_writeOnly_always0 = 0;
    f->timeSinceThrowWasCaught = 0;
    f->fielderTrackingBallState = 0;
}
```
Rolled out to `fn_3_402A8`'s **17** sites: **byte-identical codegen**, 95.03673% / 2364 B before
and after. MWCC constant-folds the compile-time-constant indices exactly as the target does.

**The idiom occurs 309 times in fielder.c, and only 17 are converted so far.** Before this session
the file contained exactly ONE `static inline` (`fielderSqrt`, line ~153). Converting the remaining
~292 sites is a large, purely-mechanical, expected-codegen-neutral readability win and is the single

it should be done in batches with a full-unit re-diff after each batch, never in one shot, and any

#### The sibling-carryover experiment: what transferred and what did not
This was run as a deliberate test of how much a decoded sibling buys you. Verdict: a great deal,
but the *dispatch tail* did not transfer at all, and assuming it would have been wrong.

CARRIED OVER verbatim:
- the 9-fielder loop skeleton (angle / distanceFromHomePlate / distanceFromLandingSpot)
- the `catchStrategyMask` 32-bit-shift-then-sign-extend packing, weights 4/2/1, and the exact same
  mask constants 0x3FFFF / 0x2DB6D / 0x12480 / 0x2
- `int` (not `s16`) for the loop counter and shiftAmt
- plain `g_Fielders[i]` indexing rather than a walking cursor
- FMA-defused dxSq/dzSq temps before `fielderSqrt`
- the inlined atan2 including its REAL BUG (`+= SANG_ANG_180` where the math wants SANG_ANG_360)
- **the catcher index-1 special case DID carry over** — `setCatcherCatchStrategy_distToLandingSpot(1)`
  vs `setFielderCatchStrategy_calcFramesToGetToDropSpot(i)`. This REFUTES the prior session's
  banked prediction that the AI path would drop it or route it through `fn_3_402A8`.

DID NOT carry over:
- The entire tail dispatch. The AI variant calls NONE of
  `selectInitialFielders_linedriveThroughPitcher` / `setInitialFielderMovements_foulBall` /
  `_generalCase` / `_DeepFly` / `chooseSecondaryFielderFromClosestOutfielder`. Instead it has its
  own INLINE line-drive-through-pitcher handler (never factored into a function) and calls the
  already-implemented `fn_3_3F24C` (foul equivalent), `fn_3_402A8` (general-case equivalent, reused
  for THREE separate mask branches), `fn_3_40D88` (DeepFly equivalent) and `fn_3_40C04` (secondary-
  fielder-selection equivalent).
- The trailing `secondaryFielderStored`/`tertiaryFielderStored` shadow-copy write does NOT exist in
  the AI variant; every path falls straight to the epilogue.
- A large pre-loop "desperation" block with NO human-side equivalent: a late-inning / tied-score /
  AI-batting-team / <=1 stored out / running-logic-bit / foul-adjacent-but-fair / high-hit check
  that sets `g_FieldingLogic.letFoulBallDropIfWinningRunOn3rdInd`. **This accounts for essentially
  the entire 56-byte size difference** between the AI (1576 B) and human (1520 B) variants — the
  size delta was correctly predictive that something structural differed, and following it found it.

### Header correction: `g_RunningLogic` offset 0x2 field width

`g_RunningLogic_s` typed offsets 0x0-0x3 as a single `u8 _00[4]`, but the target accesses offset
0x2 with `lha` (signed halfword) and tests bit mask 0x1000. Split into `u8 _00[2]; s16 _02;` —
total size unchanged at 0x20, every later field offset unchanged. This removed a
`*(s16*)((u8*)&g_RunningLogic + 2)` reinterpreting cast from the source.

**Canary: a full-project CANONICAL report diff across ALL units showed 0 of 6479 functions changed.**
Codegen-neutral everywhere, as an offset-preserving width split must be.

Naming discipline applied: the field's meaning is unknown (only that bit 0x1000 is tested in a
late-inning/tied-score AI context), so it keeps the honest `_02` placeholder rather than an invented
semantic name, and the 0x1000 mask stays a raw literal because no existing named flag enum covers it.

### `setFielderAutoMovement` inline rollout (session 41 batch)

Task 0 gate re-verified before starting: clean `ninja` (matches project-wide
baseline exactly), unit `.text` fuzzy 71.043945%, 65/223 at 100%. Per-function
table and a pre-rollout copy of `fielder.c` saved to the scratchpad for exact
revert reference.

**Surface-variant inventory** (found via a regex scan of every
`autoMovementFunctionIndex = N;` assignment, 261 raw sites total, minus the
inline's own definition body = 261 candidate occurrences of the 6-statement
idiom outside the inline itself). Distinct pointer/base surface forms found
that fit the idiom exactly (base + `.`/`->` operator, in 238 of the 261
sites once idx expressions with array/member subscripts like
`g_FieldingLogic.tertiaryFielder` and `closestFielders[j]` were handled):
`f->` (101), `fielder->` (89), `g_Fielders[N].` (24), `other->` (8),
`prior->` (5), `f0->` (3), `fielder2->` (2), `secFielder->` (1), `f2->` (1),
`f3->` (1), `f5->` (1), `bf->` (1), `cand->` (1). One of the 238 matches was
the inline definition's own body and was excluded, leaving **237 real
candidate sites**.

**Skipped as not equivalent to the idiom (23 sites)**, left untouched:
- 2 sites (`selectInitialFielders_linedriveThroughPitcher`-adjacent lines,
  actually inside `humanTeamFieldingFirstFrameAfterHit`/nearby) where the
  6-statement block is followed immediately by unrelated code, not the
  full 5-statement reset — only the index-assignment + guard is present,
  the resets never happen at that site. Not the same operation; converting
  would change behavior.
- 4 sites where an outer `if` wraps only the index-assignment + guard, but
  the 5 reset statements run unconditionally *outside* that if. Calling the
  inline would either run the resets conditionally (wrong) or run the
  index assignment unconditionally (wrong) — semantically different from
  source as written.
- 3 sites with an extra unrelated statement
  (`g_FieldingLogic.someFielderIndex = idx;`) inserted between the guard
  block and the 5 reset statements, breaking contiguity — skipped rather
  than reordered, since reordering risks visible behavior change and the
  task calls for skipping ambiguous cases.
- 12 sites that read/write through a local alias `fl->fielderAutoMovementCode[N]`
  instead of `g_FieldingLogic.fielderAutoMovementCode[N]` — likely the same
  object via a pointer alias, but not textually identical to what the inline
  hardcodes, so skipped rather than assumed equivalent.
- 2 sites where `autoMovementFunctionIndex = 0;` is followed by an entirely
  different set of field resets (`catchStrategy`, `goingToAutoLocationInd`,
  etc.) — not the idiom at all, just a coincidental leading assignment.

**Conversion mechanism used the `idx` expression already captured from the
guard block** (`g_FieldingLogic.fielderAutoMovementCode[IDX]`) as the first
inline argument, rather than trying to trace pointer-local assignments
backward — this is exactly the fielder index the original code used to
compute that same pointer, so it's provably correct without backtracking.

**Byte-identical gate turned out to be much stricter than function-count
matching in practice.** MWCC does not always re-inline `setFielderAutoMovement`
to the exact original instruction sequence at every call site — sometimes it
does (session 40's 17 sites, and most of this session's), but at some sites
the generated code differs (different register allocation), which changes
that function's size, which in turn changes the encoded displacement of any
same-file `bl` call to/from it (no ELF relocation exists for intra-TU direct
calls, so the raw branch-immediate bytes shift) — producing a *cascading*
regression in a completely unrelated calling function, not just the edited
one. This was caught by comparing all 223 functions' `fuzzy_match_percent`
after every batch, exactly as instructed, and is why per-function bisection

Investigated the 12-byte (3-instruction) shortfall. Isolated the exact

has an extra `lis r4, g_Ball@ha / addi r4, r4, g_Ball@l / lfs f1,
0x19d4(r4)` (address `g_Ball.maxYOfHit`, offset 0x19D4) immediately before
the `g_Ball.maxYOfHit < lbl_3_rodata_B64` comparison inside the

branch. Ours keeps the float value from the first `g_Ball.maxYOfHit > f8_0`
read live in `f1` and reuses it for the second comparison (legitimate CSE);
target reloads it from memory a second time, recomputing the `g_Ball` base
pointer fresh rather than reusing the register from the first access (which,
notably, target *also* recomputes fresh rather than reusing the loop's
persistent `g_Ball` pointer register — target never reuses a `g_Ball` base
pointer across statement boundaries in this whole post-loop if-chain, ours
does when it's cheap to).

Every other mismatching instruction in the function is either a branch-target
immediate (tracks relabeled blocks, not a real difference) or the identical
6-instruction-per-3-fielders register swap between {r26,r27}/{r28,r29} for
`catchStrategyMask`'s two 32-bit halves vs. the loop counters `i`/`shiftAmt`
— same phenomenon as `HandleMiddleInfieldSelection`'s swap, not fixed here
either.

flow directly (no prior source to diff against). High-level shape:
1. Early guards: `animationRelatedInd`, `updateFielderPositionAndVelocityForSpecialActions`,
   `g_Ball.deadBallReason`, then a `checkIfPlayerNeedsToMoveToCatchBall`
   dispatch when `g_FieldingLogic.locationThrownTo == 5` and `fielder->locationResponsibleForCovering == 5`.

   ladder that sets `locationResponsibleForCovering` (literal `9`, or via

   `setFielderAutoMovement(fielderIndex, 14)`, `fielderVeloAdjustmentCode = 0xb`, return.

   for a match against `fielderIndex`; on match, `locationResponsibleForCovering = i`,
   `setFielderAutoMovement(fielderIndex, 1)`, return.

### autoMovement9_OffBase_coverHome follow-up: 95.11605% -> 95.590126% (report, CANONICAL), size 1652 B -> 1624 B (target 1620 B)

Task-given hypothesis H-A (drop the `success` int flag entirely, thread every guard
straight to a single `notIntercepting:` label with a bare `return;` on the fall-through
success path) was tried and refuted: it measured 94.09383% at 1572 B (48 B under
target), worse than the 95.11605%/1652 B starting point. Disassembly comparison showed
the target still materializes the same `li r0,0/1; cmpwi r0,0; bne <epilogue>` sequence
our pre-existing `success`-flag code already produced -- the target keeps this flag in
volatile r0 because no `bl` call ever separates a `success = 0` assignment from its use,
so nothing forces a spill. Removing the flag deleted real target instructions instead of
fixing a register-allocation problem. This hypothesis was reverted back to the original
`int success` / `goto ballCheckDone` shape exactly as found in `am9_pre.c`.

The actual 32-byte-over cause was a different, untouched flag: `BOOL
coveringLocationSet`, materialized in nonvolatile r28 (`stw r28,0x10(r1)` in the
prologue, `lwz r28` in the epilogue) because it is set to TRUE before an if/elseif chain
containing three `bl setFielderLocToBeNearBase` calls, forcing its live range across
those calls. The target does not use this variable at all: each of the four
true branches jumps forward to the shared "set up covering" code, and the else (all
four false) falls through directly into loop setup. Rewriting to:

```c
if (fielder->distanceToBases[0] < lbl_3_rodata_B64) {
    fielder->locationResponsibleForCovering = 9;
} else if (fielder->distanceToBases[1] < lbl_3_rodata_B64) {
    fielder->locationResponsibleForCovering = setFielderLocToBeNearBase(fielderIndex);
} else if (fielder->distanceToBases[2] < lbl_3_rodata_B64) {
    fielder->locationResponsibleForCovering = setFielderLocToBeNearBase(fielderIndex);
} else if (fielder->distanceToBases[3] < lbl_3_rodata_B64) {
    fielder->locationResponsibleForCovering = setFielderLocToBeNearBase(fielderIndex);
} else {
    goto notCovering;
}

fielder->isResponsibleForCoveringALocation = 2;
if (fielderIndex != -1) {
    setFielderAutoMovement(fielderIndex, 14);
}
fielder->fielderVeloAdjustmentCode = 0xb;
return;

notCovering:
    ;
}
```

took the function from 95.11605% (1652 B) to 95.590126% (1624 B), eliminating the r28
prologue/epilogue save entirely and matching every instruction in this region except

else sits between that branch and the shared block), whereas our version's
last-else-is-a-plain-goto lets the compiler fold the branch-4 fallthrough straight into
the covering-work block and fold the else's goto into the preceding branch's target --

instructions in an unrelated, untouched region (the pre-existing `success` guard chain,

later guard's identical tail, an artifact ours does not reproduce). Net: 4 B over
target, versus 32 B over before this change.

#### New durable levers proven this session

1. **Match the target's ARGUMENT EVALUATION ORDER, not just the argument list.** On a mixed
   int/float call, PPC register assignment is position-independent (ints -> r3.., floats ->
   f1..), so which parameter is written first in the declaration/call does not change WHICH
   register each argument lands in -- but it DOES change the order the loads are emitted in.
   Writing `fn_3_B7E44(dist, angle)` to mirror the target's `lfs` before `lha` was worth +0.37.
2. **Constant-first comparison (`CONST > expr` instead of `expr < CONST`) is a real, measurable
   lever** and it is directional: on `autoMovement13`'s scan loop the constant-first form was
   worth +0.09 (99.438416% -> 99.53236%), and reverting it alone regressed. Cheap to sweep.
3. **Reordering the operands of a loop guard's `&&` can destroy MWCC's unrolling decision
   entirely** -- `autoMovement13`'s 9-iteration scan went 99.53% -> 88.14% and lost 4 bytes when
   `i != fielderIndex` was moved from first to second. Put the cheap index test first.
4. **The `dxSq`/`dzSq` "defuse" idiom generalises.** Splitting `fielderSqrt(dx*dx + dz*dz)` into
   two named squared temporaries prevents MWCC fusing the multiply-add into `fmadds`. This file
   already used it at a `fielderSqrt` site in `selectClosestFielderBasedOnFutureCoord`; it
   applies at ANY `fielderSqrt(a*a + b*b)` site where the target does not show `fmadds`.

### `updateFielderMovementAndPosition` -- 0.19493% -> **93.86939%** (report, CANONICAL), size 2016 B (target 2052 B, 36 B short)

Implemented from scratch off the target disassembly (0x00057BB4-0x000583B4). True leaf.
Whole-project regression gate over 6479 functions / 1340 units: **only this one function changed
anywhere**; zero regressions.

**Prototype VERIFIED CORRECT as `void updateFielderMovementAndPosition(void)`** -- NOT one of this
file's ~36 wrong-prototype cases. It reads the fielder index from `g_FieldingLogic.selectedFielder`
(0xb0), overridden by `g_Minigame.minigameRelatedIndex` (0x1923) when
`g_d_GameSettings.minigamesEnabled` (0x11) is set. The single call site is a bare `bl` with no
argument setup. No `goto` needed; every join is a natural structured fallthrough.

#### THE BIG FINDING THIS SESSION: MWCC AUTO-INLINED A NON-STATIC SINGLE-CALL-SITE CALLEE

The first landing measured only **68.5731%** and our object came out **2520 B against a 2052 B
target** -- ~115 EXTRA instructions, which turned out to be the entire body of
`updateOutfielderPositionBasedOnBallState` duplicated inline at the call site. The target keeps it
as a real `bl`.

Root cause: this file compiles with `-inline auto` (see `configure.py`), and MWCC auto-inlined a
**non-`static`, single-call-site** function. This is a DIFFERENT failure mode from the file's
well-documented "empty stub callee gets inlined away" trap -- here the callee is fully implemented
and 556 B, and MWCC inlined it anyway purely because it has exactly one call site.

Fix: bracket the **callee's own definition** in `#pragma dont_inline on` / `#pragma dont_inline reset`.
This is an established PERMANENT idiom in this repo, not scaffolding -- `fielder.c` already used it
around `fn_3_33D9C` and `fn_3_40D54` (both at 100%), and it also appears in `batter.c`
(`calculateIfHitBall`), `camera.c` (`bOD_Cam_liveBall`), `menus/text_0323C.c`, and throughout the
Dolphin SDK and Musyx. `docs/matching_notes.md` confirms `dont_inline on|off|reset` is one of the
pragmas this compiler actually accepts.

Result: **68.5731% -> 93.86939%**, our size **2520 B -> 2016 B**.
`updateOutfielderPositionBasedOnBallState` itself measured **99.78417% before AND after** -- the
pragma had ZERO effect on the callee's own codegen, so this is a free fix with no downside.

### Durable levers proven in this batch

5. **MWCC `-inline auto` will auto-inline a NON-STATIC, fully-implemented callee that has exactly
   ONE call site**, silently inflating the caller by the callee's whole body. Symptom: our object
   is hundreds of bytes OVER target and the diff shows a long run of INSERTED instructions that
   are recognisably another function's body. This is distinct from the empty-stub-inlining trap.
   **Fix: `#pragma dont_inline on` / `#pragma dont_inline reset` around the CALLEE's definition.**
   It is a permanent, established idiom in this repo (already twice in fielder.c) and it was
   measured to have ZERO effect on the callee's own codegen. Worth **+25 points** here.
   Before opening a hypothesis log on any caller that comes out much LARGER than target, check
   for this first.
6. **The conditional-override idiom beats `if/else` where the target preloads the "then" value
   and branches over the else**: `x = A; if (cond) x = B;` instead of `if (!cond) x = A; else x = B;`.
   Worth **+2.0 points** on `autoMovement14` -- the single biggest step there. Both polarities
   should be measured; this complements the already-documented "explicit if/else beats a ternary"
   lever rather than contradicting it (ternary -> if/else -> conditional-override is the ladder).
7. **`fielderSqrt(a*a + b*b)` operand order must be measured PER SITE.** On `autoMovement14`
   three separate sites each gained ~0.04 from flipping `(dz*dz + dx*dx)` to `(dx*dx + dz*dz)`,
   and on `autoMovement13` the opposite direction won. There is no global right answer.
8. **A callee defined textually LATER in fielder.c is not visible** and silently needs a
   file-scope forward declaration. Bit `autoMovement14` (`checkForBufferedThrow`). When landing a
   new function, check every callee's definition line number against the new function's line
   number BEFORE building.

### Durable levers proven in this batch (continuing the numbering)

9. **THE PERSISTENT-REGISTER-COUNT LEVER (the session's most valuable finding).** When a function
   lands at exact-or-near-exact size but a LOW score (~50-90%) with mismatches spread near-uniformly
   across the whole body and classified `DIFF_ARG_MISMATCH`, the cause is almost always that our
   code persists FEWER long-lived values in nonvolatile registers than the target does.
   **Diagnostic: compare our prologue's `stw r2x,...(r1)` save list against the target's, and
   identify what each register holds.** Two concrete fixes, both measured:
   (a) Add a function-scope pointer local to create the missing persistent base
       (`InMemFielder* pitcher = &g_Fielders[0];`) -- +3.155 on `autoMovement1_coverBase`. It must
       be at FUNCTION scope; branch scope scored 0.25 lower.
   (b) **The re-materialization mapping.** Where the target keeps a BYTE-OFFSET register
       (`mulli rN, rIndex, 0x268`) live and rebuilds the address at specific sites via
       `lis g_Fielders@ha; addi r0,...; add rM, r0, rN` instead of reusing the live element
       pointer, write THOSE sites (and only those) as plain `g_Fielders[idx].field` array
       indexing while keeping `fielder->field` everywhere the target reuses the live base.
       Worth +2.6 across two sites on `autoMovement11`, taking it to an EXACT-size 99.55%.
   **Do NOT over-apply (b):** converting ALL accesses to array indexing scored 43.1% on
   `autoMovement1` (a 12-point catastrophic regression). It is a per-site mapping, not a global
   style choice.
10. **A higher score at the WRONG size is not progress.** On `autoMovement11`, adding a duplicated
    `else` clause scored 93.85% but put the object 60 B OVER target; it was a misdiagnosis of a
    compiler code-motion as a missing source `else`, and was reverted in favour of the `goto`
    form that reached the exact size and 99.55%. **Always read OUR true size from
    `objdiff-cli diff` alongside the percent** -- note the `size` field in `report generate`
    output is the TARGET's size, not ours, and has been misread as an exact-size match before.
11. **An apparently-dead store may not be dead to the compiler.** Removing
    `wallJumpApexY = ballY - const` (provably overwritten on every later path) REGRESSED
    `wallJumpInitialization` by 1.2 points. Transcribe redundant-looking stores as the target has
    them and only remove one if removal measures better.
12. **MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY -- RESOLVED.** A worker mid-session suspected that standalone
    `objdiff-cli report generate` returns stale results and that only the `ninja`-driven
    `build/GYQE01/report.json` is trustworthy. This was **independently re-tested and DISPROVED**:
    the two agree exactly at both baseline and final state. Either is canonical. The same worker
    also reported 67 functions at 100% in this unit; that was **wrong** -- a direct count of the
    unit's `functions` list with `fuzzy_match_percent == 100.0` gives **65**, agreeing with the
    `measures` block's `matched_functions`.

    Read which one the target uses before writing either.

    `li r5,0x0` and was part of the same +85-point step. Where the target sets a flag's default
    early, set it early in the C too.

    PER-FUNCTION measurement, not a file-wide rule.** `autoMovement14_infieldSupport` needed three

flow is `if`/`else` plus early returns.

#### PROTOTYPE CORRECTED (real correctness fix -- running tally now ~41)

Was `void checkForAndSetFielderWallActionsOrDives(void)` in both the header and fielder.c.
**Both WRONG.** Evidence: `mr r29, r3` at entry then `mulli r5, r29, 0x268`; every exit path sets
r3 to 0 or 1; the sole call site at `0x0002CA78` does
`mr r3, r28; bl checkForAndSetFielderWallActionsOrDives; cmpwi r3, 0x0`.
Now: **`int checkForAndSetFielderWallActionsOrDives(int fielderIndex);`**, corrected in both.

#### THE AUTO-INLINE TRAP FIRED -- AND WAS PREDICTED IN ADVANCE

`divingCatch`, `wallJumpInitialization` and `clamberInitialization` each had **zero** call sites in
the TU before this function existed. Implementing this function gave each of them **exactly one**,
which is precisely MWCC `-inline auto`'s trigger condition. All three were wrapped in
`#pragma dont_inline on` / `#pragma dont_inline reset`. Verified afterwards: `divingCatch`
64.37905%, `wallJumpInitialization` 32.19168%, `clamberInitialization` 100% -- **all three
completely unchanged** by the pragma, confirming again that it has zero effect on the callee's own
codegen. fielder.c now uses this idiom 6 times.

**GENERALISED RULE (new durable lever 18):** implementing a caller can retroactively spring the
auto-inline trap on callees that were previously never called. **Whenever you implement a function,
check whether any of its callees previously had ZERO call sites in the TU** -- if so, pre-emptively
wrap those callees in `#pragma dont_inline on`/`reset` before you even build.

### CROSS-FILE CORRECTNESS FIX: `InputStruct._08` was signed, should be unsigned

`include/game/UnknownHomes_Game.h` declared `InputStruct._08` as `s16`. The target copies it with
**`lhz`** (zero-extend), not `lha` (sign-extend) — so the field is UNSIGNED. Corrected to `u16`.
Checked every other user of `InputStruct` project-wide first (only `batter.c` pointer uses, which
do not depend on signedness). Result: `atBat_Fielders` went to 100%, and **`fn_3_2E41C` improved
82.22857% -> 83.72143% as a free side effect** because it performs the identical `_08` copy.
Project-wide matched functions 1824 -> 1825, zero regressions.

**Generalised: the `lhz`/`lha` opcode is direct evidence of a struct field's SIGNEDNESS, not just
its width.** The existing rule "read the width off the access opcode" should be extended: `lha` =>
signed 16-bit, `lhz` => unsigned 16-bit, `lbz` => unsigned 8-bit, `lbzx`+`extsb` => signed 8-bit.
A mismatch here costs exactly one instruction per access and is easy to miss. This is the second
signedness bug found in this file (the first was `baseCurrentlyOn` declared `u8` while using -1 as
a sentinel).

### `#pragma inline_max_auto_size` FAMILY IS A SILENT NO-OP IN THIS TOOLCHAIN — REFUTED, do not retry

Tested to close `updateFielder_SpecificValuesEachFrame`'s missing inlined copy of `fn_3_555AC`.
Swept N = 50/100/150/250/400 bracketing the CALLER; also tried `#pragma inline on` on the callee,
and `extra_cflags=["-inline deferred,auto"]` on the unit. **Every variant produced byte-identical
output.**

**The decisive control: a DELIBERATELY MISSPELLED pragma name (`inline_max_auto_size_TYPO_TEST`)
compiled silently, with no warning, and produced byte-identical output to the correctly-spelled
one.** This toolchain does not diagnose unknown pragmas, so "it compiled" proves nothing — the
whole `inline_max_*` family is simply ignored. Note this does NOT generalise to all pragmas:
`#pragma dont_inline on/reset` demonstrably works. Reuse the misspelling control before trusting
any new pragma in this project.

Unit cflags confirmed for the record: `-O4,p -sym on -inline deferred -requireprotos
-fp_contract on -lang=c`, `mw_version = "GC/2.6"`. `cflags_base`'s `-inline auto` is overridden by
`cflags_rel`'s `-inline deferred`.

### `fn_3_555AC` — the target contains TWO textual copies; hand-duplicate, never use `inline`

`updateFielder_SpecificValuesEachFrame` was 292 B SHORT, dominated by a ~328 B block: the target
holds BOTH the standalone `fn_3_555AC` (356 B) AND an inlined copy of its body at 0x56C78-0x56DC4.

- Marking `fn_3_555AC` with the **`inline` keyword** DID close the gap, **but destroyed the
  standalone symbol** (vague linkage => MWCC drops the out-of-line body), regressing `fn_3_555AC`
  98.03371% -> unmatched, for a NET LOSS. Refuted.
- **What worked: hand-duplicating the body as inline C at the call site, leaving `fn_3_555AC`'s
  own definition completely untouched.** `updateFielder_SpecificValuesEachFrame` 85.12862% ->
  **91.55962%**, going from 292 B SHORT to 52 B OVER. `fn_3_555AC` stayed at 98.03371%.

**Key enabling fact, worth remembering generally:** a non-static global function's out-of-line body
is emitted by MWCC whether or not anything calls it. `fn_3_555AC` was already scoring 98.03371%
with ZERO call sites. So removing a function's last call site is SAFE for its own symbol — which
makes hand-inlining a free move whenever the target shows duplication.

The two copies were confirmed logically identical; the inlined one only differs by reusing the
enclosing function's already-resident `fielder` base pointer instead of recomputing it.

  `lockedOutInd`, writing `x = A || B;` compiled branchless; `x = 0; if (A || B) x = 1;` reproduced
  the target's `beq`/`li`/`stb`/`b`/`li`/`stb`. Worth +0.15.

  directly; replacing the flag with a compound `if (A || B || C)` fixed it on

### Root cause of the 28 B overshoot — DIAGNOSED AND CONFIRMED, but not yet fixable

We hoist `lbl_3_rodata_B20` (0.0f) into the nonvolatile **f31** across the 9-fielder loop.
That forces a 0x30 frame instead of the target's 0x20, plus `stfd f31`/`psq_st` in the
prologue and `psq_l`/`lfd f31` in the epilogue — 4 extra instructions / 16 B — plus a
register-shuffle cascade at the loop preheader (an extra `mr r28, r0`).

The target does NOT hoist: it reloads `lbl_3_rodata_B20` inside the loop body immediately
after the `bl ballDistCalculator`, so the constant never occupies a nonvolatile. The target's
real source almost certainly wrote a plain `0.0f` literal, which MWCC rematerializes freely;
our `extern const f32` declaration makes it a loop-invariant *memory* load that LICM hoists.

Corroborating evidence in the same function: at target row 113 the sqrt guard constant is
`lbl_3_rodata_B20` — i.e. the target's pooled `0.0f` from `dolsqrtf2`'s inline body DEDUPED
with the same pooled `0.0f` used by the velocity compare. Ours emits an anonymous `@8775`
there, because our `lbl_3_rodata_B20` is an `SHN_UNDEF` extern and so nothing can dedupe
against it. Same for `dolsqrtf2`'s three double constants: target
`lbl_3_rodata_B30`/`B38`/`B40` vs ours `@8776`/`@8777`/`@8778`.

**DURABLE LEVER 19 (new): the `extern const f32 lbl_3_rodata_XXXX` trick has a hidden cost.**
Declaring a pooled float as `extern const` (rather than writing the literal) makes it a
loop-invariant *memory* operand, which MWCC's LICM will hoist into a nonvolatile FPR across
a loop containing a call — forcing an f31 save/restore and a bigger stack frame that the
target does not have. The target, having written a literal, rematerializes it instead.
Symptom to recognise: our function is ~16 B over, has `stfd f31`/`psq_st` + `psq_l`/`lfd f31`
in prologue/epilogue and a 0x10-larger frame, and the target reloads the same
`lbl_3_rodata_XXXX` inside the loop. Dropping `const` fixes THAT function and breaks many
others, so it is not a usable file-wide fix. A per-function fix is still an OPEN PROBLEM —
a block-scope `extern f32` redeclaration is a type-compatibility violation and was not tried.
Second cost of the same trick: because the extern is `SHN_UNDEF` in our object, MWCC cannot
dedupe other pooled uses of the same value against it (e.g. `dolsqrtf2`'s inlined `0.0`),
so we emit anonymous `@NNNN` pool entries where the target reuses the named label.

**Decision: `liveBallFielderControlAITeam` left at 84.35555% and moved off.** At 720 B it is
0.34% of the file; closing it fully is worth ~+0.05 points, far less than the FREE-stub queue.
Not marked `exhausted` — hypothesis [2] shows a real, understood path, it just needs a
per-function scoping mechanism that does not exist yet.

### ENVIRONMENT — root cause of the `orig/GYQE01/sys/main.dol` corruption FOUND

Session 44 logged this as "suspect a backup/sync/AV agent". That was wrong. It is
**`E:\Project Rio\MSSB Editor`'s pytest suite** (`tests/test_game.py`, including a test named
`test_replace_restore_is_exact`) using THIS repo's `orig\GYQE01\` directory as a live test
fixture. It repeatedly rewrites `orig\GYQE01\sys\main.dol` (and `files\aaaa.dat`,
`files\ZZZZ.dat`), and leaves an `orig\GYQE01\files\_mssb_editor_backup\` folder containing
`journal.json` / `overrides.json` — that folder is the forensic fingerprint to look for.

Evidence chain: (a) the ISO is GOOD — extracting it to a directory OUTSIDE the repo yields
`main.dol` = `8a7f951cd701a9db6ed13a0bd59456d7a44b6fbb` every time; (b) restoring the file
inside `orig/` and re-hashing 30 s later showed it reverted to
`bb18a495aa5be9fcb0882a09e57993b702e13e09` on its own; (c) `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`
showed `python.exe -m pytest tests/test_game.py` running during exactly those windows; (d) the
three RELs (`game.rel`/`menus.rel`/`debug.rel`) were NEVER corrupted — only `sys/` and the
two `.dat` files.

**Recovery recipe that works:** keep a verified extraction outside the repo
(`dtk.exe disc extract "<iso>" <some-dir-outside-the-repo>`), then
`Copy-Item -Force "<that-dir>\sys\*" "orig\GYQE01\sys\"` and immediately run `ninja`.
Do NOT bypass with `mwcceppc.exe`. Do NOT kill the user's pytest process — poll
`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='python.exe'"` for a command line matching
`pytest|test_game` and wait for ~80 s of quiet (no process AND stable `main.dol` mtime)
before restoring, otherwise the restore is immediately undone.

Attempting to sidestep this by redirecting `config/GYQE01/config.yml`'s `object:` paths at a
private uncontended copy of the disc files was BLOCKED by the permission system as a
shared-resource modification. Waiting it out is the sanctioned approach.

**This is a standing hazard, not a one-off.** It cost this session roughly half its wall
clock across three separate stalls. Worth telling the user to point MSSB Editor's test
fixture at its own scratch directory instead of the decomp's `orig/`.

```
**IMPORTANT correction to the LEVER-18 reasoning, for future sessions:** a worker initially
refused this task on the grounds that `fn_3_2EA88` has ZERO call sites of its own (its only
target caller, `miniGameDash`, is still a bare stub in our C), and therefore concluded the
inline trap could not fire. That reasoning is WRONG. MWCC's `-inline auto` heuristic counts
call sites of the CALLEE within the translation unit; it does not care whether the enclosing
caller is itself ever called. Implementing an uncalled function still creates live call sites
for everything IT calls. Always apply the LEVER-18 check to the callees of any function you
implement, regardless of whether that function has callers.

**Also note** the call-graph doc's `callees=` / `all_callees=` lists are derived from the
TARGET disassembly, not from our C. So `miniGameDash`'s listed callees do not exist as text in
our source while it is still a stub. Do not treat a missing call site as a stale call graph.
```

```
**Residual 16 B short / 9.2% — DIAGNOSED, and it is a NEW and interesting lever.**
Both stick-history loops matched (the descending `charHist[i-1]` copy is an identical
`bdnz` loop; the 20-entry copy-back is identically FULLY unrolled; the `-1` fill is identically
unrolled to 17 inline `sth`s plus a `bdnz` remainder). The gap is that **the target emits a
DEAD loop-entry guard before two of those loops and we do not**:

```
li   r8, 0x1        <- materialise the loop variable's INITIAL value
cmpwi r8, 0x14      <- compare against the constant bound 20
bge  <past the loop>  <- provably never taken

```
and again before the copy-back loop with `li r0, 0x0 / cmpwi r0, 0x14 / bge`. It then

variable, so it emitted its generic guard+remainder skeleton with the constants only partially
folded. Our build folds them away entirely. Something about the original source kept the
induction variable opaque. UNTRIED ideas, best first:

    residual. If it does, this is one shared root cause worth solving once for both; if that

    the shared `i` that the 9-fielder loop also uses — or the exact reverse, since the sibling
    reuses one `j` for all of its loops.
(c) Declare the loop variable `volatile`-free but assign it from something opaque first — less
    likely to be the original source, try last.
```

function's `for (j = 1; j < 20; j++)` reset loop and `for (j = 0; j < 20; j++)` copy-back loop,
and our build omits both, exactly as in `minigameDashUpdateFieldingVariables`.

jumps directly from `162740 li r6, -0x1` to `162744 li r9, 0x13` with nothing in between.)


The remainder-trip-count re-materialisation (`li r9, 0x13` / `subfic r0, r9, 0x14` for the

**Method note worth keeping:** in this project's `report generate` JSON, a unit's canonical
`.text` number is `units[].measures.fuzzy_match_percent`, which for this unit is numerically
identical to `units[].sections[".text"].fuzzy_match_percent` (because `total_code` == the
`.text` section size, this unit having no other code section). Both read 84.080986 in the
session-46 baseline, matching the historical figure, so either key is safe to quote — but
`measures.matched_code_percent` (13.59%) is an EXACT-byte metric, NOT the fuzzy one, and must
never be quoted as the match percentage. When two readings disagree, re-read the JSON rather
than averaging or trusting the later one.

### THE session-46 finding worth carrying to other files

**A bare stub is very often a near-verbatim copy of a function that is ALREADY WRITTEN in the
same file. Grep before you decode.** All four functions this session were largely assembled
from two existing in-tree blocks rather than derived from scratch:
- `liveBallFielderControlHumanTeam:8715-8747` — the 9-fielder `updateFielderDirectionFacing` /
  `ballDistCalculator` / xz-movement-dir loop plus the
  `fielding_handleCollisionsAndSpecialActions` + minigame-vs-`fielderWBallIndex` `dolsqrtf2`
  tail. Reused VERBATIM by all three `minigameDash*`/`fn_3_2EA88` functions.
- `fn_3_2E41C:3706-3759` — the entire control-stick-history block (characterIndex ->
  control/charHist derivation, descending history copy, `-1` fill, `currentStickDirection`
  select, 20-entry copy-back, the three `g_FieldingLogic.fielderInputs` stores, and the
  `dashPtr`/`jumpDiveStruct` pointer arithmetic). Reused by
  `minigameDashUpdateFieldingVariables` and `miniGameDash`.

The sibling block is worth more than speed: it independently CONFIRMS readings you would
otherwise distrust. `fn_3_2E41C:3742-3743` proved that the `currentStickDirection` guard's
second operand really is `== 0` and not `< 0`, which is the opposite of what the structurally
identical guard in `liveBallFielderControlHumanTeam:8834` uses. Without the sibling I would
probably have "corrected" the disassembly to match the other function and lost points.

### Second finding: LEVER 18 applies to a function with ZERO callers of its own

A worker refused a task on the grounds that `fn_3_2EA88` has no call sites, so implementing it
could not spring the single-call-site inline trap on its callees. That is WRONG and cost a
round trip. MWCC's `-inline auto` counts call sites of the CALLEE within the translation unit;
it does not care whether the enclosing caller is itself ever called. Implementing a
completely-uncalled function still creates live call sites for everything IT calls. Run the
LEVER-18 check on the callees of every function you implement, unconditionally.

Corollary that also confused that worker: the call-graph doc's `callees=` / `all_callees=`
lists are derived from the TARGET disassembly, not from our C. A stub's listed callees do not
exist as text in our source. A missing call site is NOT evidence of a stale call graph.

### Third finding (OPEN, now with two data points): the dead-loop-guard residual

MWCC's target build emits a provably-dead loop-entry guard before certain 20-trip unrolled
loops that our build folds away:
```
li    rN, <init>      <- materialise the induction variable's INITIAL value
cmpwi rN, 0x14        <- compare against the literal bound 20
bge   <past the loop> <- provably never taken
```
Confirmed in BOTH `minigameDashUpdateFieldingVariables` (before the `-1` fill loop AND before
the 20-entry copy-back loop) and, independently, in `fn_3_2E41C` (83.72143%, 1100 vs 1120,
20 B short) at the same two loops. **Two independent occurrences of the identical idiom means
this is a shared, loop-shape-driven codegen cause, not context-specific** — solving it once
should lift both functions, and it is worth real effort because it is currently the single
largest identified residual in either.

Already-refuted approach: giving each loop its own declared `int` variable. Session 11's
"MWCC normalises loop-variable IDENTITY" finding shows this compiles byte-identically; that
build was deliberately NOT repeated this session. Do not propose it again.

Untried ideas: (a) make the loop bound non-literal (a `const int` or an enum constant) so the
unroller cannot fold the guard; (b) write the loops as `while` with the increment in the body;
(c) check whether the target's `-inline deferred` ordering means these loops were unrolled in a
DIFFERENT pass than ours; (d) compare against a third, already-100% function elsewhere in the
repo that contains a 20-trip unrolled loop, to see which source form reproduces the guard.

### THE session-47 finding worth carrying to other files

**The "grep for an existing sibling before decoding" lever now has its strongest data point yet, and
it generalises one level further: the sibling to look for is often an already-written `static inline`
HELPER, not a whole function.**

`decideHowToTrackFoulBall` is 4840 B and had no structurally close whole-function sibling. But nearly
its entire body turned out to be repeated hand-inlined instances of the *existing*
`fielderTrackingBall_applyIntendedLocation` static-inline helper already defined in this file — each
instance called with a different computed (x, z) target pair. Recognising the helper's codegen
signature in the disassembly (learned from `fielderTrackingBall_updateVariables` earlier the same
session) collapsed a 4840 B decode into: one early-return reset gate, a three-way branch selecting
between three target formulas, a 6-iteration future-landing-spot search loop, and a shared tail.
0.08% -> 84.79% in a single implementation attempt.

The practical procedure: when a big stub's disassembly shows the same 15-30 instruction block
repeating many times with only its inputs changing, stop decoding it as straight-line code and go
looking for the `static inline` helper that emits exactly that block. This file has at least three
(`fielderSqrt`, `setFielderAutoMovement`, `fielderTrackingBall_applyIntendedLocation`).

### Second finding: `g_Fielders[0]` vs `fielder->` is decided by ONE instruction, and it is worth checking

A hardcoded `g_Fielders[0]` inside a per-fielder function looks like a decode error, and a semantic
probe was run on `autoMovement4_AI_goTowardsHitBall`'s reset block to correct it to `fielder->`.
**The probe REGRESSED it, 99.67836% -> 93.391815%, and was reverted.** The disassembly is decisive
and unambiguous: that block loads its base with a bare `lis r4, g_Fielders@ha` /
`lfsu f3, g_Fielders@l(r4)` and never adds the `mulli r?, r30, 0x268` index register anywhere near
the store sequence. It really is `g_Fielders[0]`.

The contrast is what makes this durable: `autoMovement21_23_humanControlInitialSelectedFielders` has a
*visually identical* reset block that DOES do `add r4, r0, r28` first — and there it genuinely is
`fielder->`. Two neighbouring functions, same seven-store block, different answers. Read the
base-address instructions at every site; never generalise one site's answer to another.
